html:
A legal board of three men, Octavian, Mark Antony and Lepidus, set up by law on 27 November 43 BCE to rule Rome with near absolute power. Unlike the First Triumvirate, it was an official office.

Its first act was a new round of proscriptions: lists of enemies who could be killed for a reward and whose property was seized. Hundreds of senators and many wealthy men died. Antony insisted on including Cicero, who was hunted down and killed. The money paid for the war against Caesar's killers, who were beaten at Philippi in 42 BCE.

The triumvirs then split the Roman world. Antony took the rich east, Octavian the west with Italy, and Lepidus Africa. Octavian fought Sextus Pompey, who held Sicily and blocked Rome's grain. The pact was renewed for five years in 37 BCE. In 36 BCE Lepidus tried to take Sicily for himself, his troops deserted him, and Octavian pushed him out.

The board expired at the end of 33 BCE, and the rivalry between Octavian and Antony turned into the war that ended at Actium. Octavian went on to become Augustus.
sum: A legal board of three men, Octavian, Mark Antony and Lepidus, set up by law on 27 November 43 BCE to rule Rome with near absolute power. Unlike the First Triumvirate, it was an official office.
